speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Four outer strokes — half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved — then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person attained; after which speech ends.
premises: Four outer strokes: half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved.
Then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person.
After which speech ends: what more is to be said?
inference: Portrait, then vision, then silence: recognition completes itself.
uncertainties: Whether the triple-throb state (trispandabhāva) is breath or consciousness is unresolved.
